title: Sales Foundations
content: Sales is helping a prospect solve a problem through your offering in exchange for value. People buy to move away from pain or toward gain — emotion decides, logic justifies. KEY CONCEPTS: The buyer's journey (awareness, consideration, decision). The difference between features (what it is) and benefits (what it does for them). Building rapport and trust as the foundation of every sale. WORKED EXAMPLE: A prospect says 'just looking.' Instead of pitching, ask 'What prompted you to look today?' — uncovering the trigger event. PRACTICE: 1) List 3 benefits (not features) of a product you know. 2) Write 3 open-ended discovery questions. 3) Identify the pain behind a recent purchase you made.

title: The Sales Process
content: The 7-stage process: Prospecting, Connect, Discovery, Presentation, Objection Handling, Closing, Follow-up. Master the flow and never skip discovery. KEY CONCEPTS: ICP (Ideal Customer Profile) for targeting. Qualifying with BANT (Budget, Authority, Need, Timeline). The rule of talking 30%, listening 70%. WORKED EXAMPLE: Qualifying call — 'Who else is involved in a decision like this?' reveals authority and stakeholders early. PRACTICE: 1) Map your ICP's top 3 traits. 2) Write a BANT qualifying question for each letter. 3) Role-play a 5-question discovery opener.

title: Discovery Mastery — SPIN
content: SPIN questioning: Situation (context), Problem (difficulties), Implication (consequences), Need-payoff (value of solving). Drive the pain funnel from surface complaint to quantified impact. KEY CONCEPTS: Implication questions create urgency by exposing the cost of inaction. Self-persuasion — buyers who articulate their own pain own the solution. WORKED EXAMPLE: 'If this delay continues another quarter, what does it cost you?' turns a mild problem into a priority. PRACTICE: 1) Write one question of each SPIN type for a real deal. 2) Practice the pain funnel on a colleague. 3) Quantify a prospect's problem in dollars.

title: Objection Handling
content: Objections are requests for information, not rejection. Framework: Acknowledge, Clarify, Respond, Confirm. KEY CONCEPTS: 'Too expensive' means value is unclear, not budget absent — reframe to ROI and cost of inaction. The five objection classes: price, timing, authority, competitor, status quo. Status quo (doing nothing) is the hardest and most common. WORKED EXAMPLE: 'It's too expensive' → 'Compared to what?' surfaces the real reference point. PRACTICE: 1) Script an Acknowledge-Clarify-Respond-Confirm for a price objection. 2) List your top 3 objections and a reframe for each.

title: Closing & Methodologies
content: Closing techniques: assumptive, summary, alternative, urgency, question close. Never close before value is established. KEY CONCEPTS: The trial close tests readiness mid-conversation. Methodologies: Challenger (teach-tailor-take control), Sandler (equal footing, upfront contracts), Solution selling. WORKED EXAMPLE: Summary close — recap the three agreed values, then 'Shall we get started?' PRACTICE: 1) Write a summary close for a real deal. 2) Practice a trial close question. 3) Identify which methodology fits your market.

title: Enterprise & Multi-Stakeholder
content: Complex B2B deals involve buying committees: champion, economic buyer, technical buyer, blocker. Master MEDDIC (Metrics, Economic buyer, Decision criteria, Decision process, Identify pain, Champion). KEY CONCEPTS: Build ROI business cases the champion sells internally for you. Mutual action plans. Navigate procurement, legal, security gates. WORKED EXAMPLE: Coaching a champion — give them a one-page business case to forward to the economic buyer. PRACTICE: 1) Map stakeholders on a live deal. 2) Build a simple ROI model. 3) Draft a mutual action plan.

title: Grandmaster — Revenue Architecture
content: Architect revenue engines, not just close deals. Design processes, comp plans, enablement that scale. KEY CONCEPTS: Pipeline math — coverage ratios (3-4x quota), velocity, capacity models. Forecast discipline (commit/best-case/pipeline). Coach and multiply other sellers. Shape buying visions before an RFP exists. WORKED EXAMPLE: Diagnosing a team's pipeline — low coverage means prospecting problem, low win-rate means qualification problem. PRACTICE: 1) Calculate needed pipeline coverage for a quota. 2) Design a 3-stage sales process. 3) Write a coaching plan for a struggling rep.

title: King Level — Market Making
content: Operate as a market-maker. Create categories and demand that didn't exist. Command boardroom trust and shape industries. KEY CONCEPTS: Category creation — define the problem the market didn't know it had. Build sales cultures and philosophies others study. Turn selling into value creation so complete customers evangelize unprompted. At King level, the market moves toward you because you redefined winning. WORKED EXAMPLE: A company reframes 'CRM software' as 'customer success platform' — creating a new category it owns. PRACTICE: 1) Reframe your product as a new category. 2) Define the vision you want your market to adopt. 3) Design how customers become evangelists.
